source_text: Te ergo apparet non studuisse ut obiecta refelleres; sed ut patrono tuo, ad quem scribebas, miserabiliter illuderes; putaretque te rude quidpiam detulisse quod iure morderes; cum id iam superiorum concessione et corporum institutione laudasses.
pass_a_gloss: You therefore appear not to have studied to refute the objections; but miserably to mock your patron to whom you were writing; and he would think you had brought something raw which you might rightly bite; when you had already praised it by the concession of the earlier things and by the institution of bodies.
pass_b_english: It is therefore clear that you did not strive to refute the objections, but to deceive miserably the patron to whom you were writing. You wanted him to think you had brought forward some crude statement that you could rightly bite at, although you had already praised it by conceding the preceding points and the divine institution of bodies.

choices.english: sense taken from the locked Augustinus.it Latin
choices.why: Load-bearing wording in Julian's Latin; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
